tagline: Shared git hooks for ticket-based workflows, JIRA-style by default.
description: Shared git hooks for ticket-based workflows: a ticket prefix in commit messages, a branch name check, protected branches and an automatic version bump after a merge. The ticket key is JIRA-style (ABC-123) by default and the pattern is configurable.
keywords: git, git hooks, githooks, jira, commit message, branch name, versioning, inebhedj
overview: ih-cgh is a set of shared git hooks for projects that put a ticket key in branch names and commit messages. By default the key is JIRA-style (ABC-123), but the pattern is configurable, so it does not depend on JIRA. The hooks are copied into your repository's .githooks directory and activated with core.hooksPath, so they are committed with your code and every clone runs the same version.
featCommitMsg: commit-msg: puts the ticket key of the branch name in front of the commit subject (with the default settings ABC-123: Fix it, or NOJIRA: ... when there is no ticket).
featPreCommit: pre-commit: checks the branch name (with the default settings ABC-123-some-topic or NOJIRA-some-topic) and asks for confirmation before a commit to a protected branch (master or main by default).
featPostMerge: post-merge: after a git merge into master or main (configurable), a branch whose name ends with -version-major, -version-minor, -version-patch or -version-fix bumps the npm version, tags it and pushes (Node projects).
featMultiple: Several scripts per hook: every hook runs the scripts of its hooks.d directory in order, so you can add your own next to ours.
installCloneIntro: Run the installer from the repository you want to set up. Any clone of this repository will do; there is no need to keep it inside your project.
installTeamText: After cloning, the committed hooks only need to be enabled (the installer does the same, and also updates them):
installNpmIntro: In a Node project you can add the package and let npm install set up the hooks.
installNpmNote: cgh prepare installs quietly. It does nothing on CI servers (when CI is set), outside of git repositories or with CGH_SKIP_INSTALL=1, and it never makes npm install fail. Other commands: cgh install, cgh uninstall, cgh check, cgh version.
installOptionsIntro: Running the installer again updates the hooks. Your cgh.conf and your own scripts are never overwritten.
optDryRun: Show what would happen, change nothing.
configIntro: The file is .githooks/cgh.conf, with one key = value per line. Every value can also be set with git config cgh.<key-with-dashes> or with the environment variable CGH_<KEY>, which take precedence.
cfgTicketRegex: An extended regular expression that matches a ticket key. The default accepts keys such as ABC-123 (capital letters or digits, a hyphen and a number). Change it to use another ticket format.
cfgNoTicket: The token used when there is no ticket.
cfgBranchRegex: An extended regular expression that every new branch name has to match.
cfgProtectedBranches: Space separated globs, for example release/*. The value none protects nothing.
cfgVersionBranches: Space separated globs: a merge into these branches can bump the version.
cfgVersionPush: Set no to not push the version commit and the tag.
configCustomText: The default ticket key is JIRA-style, so a branch such as PROJ_12-fix-it or #123-fix-it is rejected until you change ticket_regex. Two examples of other formats (the branch name has to start with the key):
hookJiraPrefix: Takes the ticket from the start of the branch name and prepends it to the commit subject. The body and comments are left alone. Nothing happens if the subject already starts with a ticket, for fixup and squash commits, merges, rebases, cherry-picks and a detached HEAD.
hookBranchName: A new branch (one without commits of its own) whose name does not match branch_regex is rejected, with a suggestion how to rename it. An old branch with a bad name only gets a notice.
hookProtectedBranch: Asks for confirmation before a commit to a protected branch. Without a terminal (IDE, scripts) the commit is rejected, unless you override it explicitly.
hookVersionBump: After a git merge into a version branch it looks at the branches that point at the merged commit and bumps the version if one of them ends with -version-major, -version-minor, -version-patch or -version-fix.
protectedText: To commit to a protected branch without a terminal, override the check explicitly:
versionTitle: Bumping the version with a merge
versionText: If several branches match, the highest bump wins. The hook runs npm version (commit NOJIRA: Releasing version X, tag vX) and pushes the commit and the tag together, so either both arrive or neither.
skipNoVerify: Skips pre-commit and commit-msg as usual. Client-side hooks can always be bypassed, so enforce important rules in CI as well.
skipCghSkip: Skips all scripts of ih-cgh for one command.
skipCghDebug: Prints every script that is run.
ownHooksText: Put an executable script into .githooks/hooks.d/<hook-name>/ and run the installer again, which creates the missing stub for that hook. For example:
ownHooksNote: Scripts run in lexical order and the first one that fails stops the hook. Files ending in .sample, .backup or .disabled are ignored. A script gets the hook's arguments and its standard input. A hook that already existed in .git/hooks when you installed keeps running after the custom scripts.
serverText: Client-side hooks can be skipped, so the installer also puts .githooks/cgh-check into your repository (cgh check from npm). It checks the branch name and the subject of every commit in BASE..HEAD with the same configuration as the hooks:
notesRequirements: The hooks are POSIX shell scripts. The tests need only git and a POSIX shell, and each runs in a fresh temporary repository.
